A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CATCH and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably across the reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, parameter-sensitivity experiments, and anomaly-score case studies in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ASD results, TFAD comparisons, and controlled frequency-specific experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Frequency patching, mask generation, masked attention, the four loss components, alternating optimization, and point-aligned scoring are retained. CCD and TFRM receive clearer organization and explanation. Algorithm 1 re-expresses relative loss weights with a unit-weight time term, without establishing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within the existing multivariate anomaly-detection task: v2 adds ASD application-server data and four synthetic conditions involving low-, medium-, high-frequency, and non-band-separated anomalies. The original nine real-world datasets and twelve TODS datasets remain.

E2.justification: TFAD changes from a related-work citation into an evaluated comparator, increasing the main comparison from fourteen to fifteen baselines. Its results appear in v2 Table 2 and Appendix C. The original comparator set remains.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a controlled four-condition frequency evaluation. Appendix A.4 specifies configurations for newly evaluated TFAD, including TCN-depth and kernel-count searches. Existing metrics and reported dataset lengths remain unchanged; newly disclosed configurations for retained baselines do not establish that their experiments changed.

E4.justification: New Appendix D systematically tests the central frequency-modeling rationale across four spectral conditions, comparing CATCH with ModernTCN, iTransformer, DualTF, and TFAD in Table 12. The earlier component ablations, sensitivity studies, and Appendix B case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Added result rows continue the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets for ASD, TFAD, and the four spectral conditions. CATCH reports ASD Affiliated-F1/AUC-ROC of 0.804/0.824 and high-frequency-condition scores of 0.915/0.987. All matched per-dataset values are unchanged. Aggregate win counts are revised, including CATCH's ROC-family count from 57 to 65, although the latter conflicts with displayed results.

T1.justification: The underlying mathematical formulation is retained. Separately displayed reconstruction and anomaly-score equations restate operations already described in v1; neither version adds formal theoretical guarantees, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain frequency patching, adaptive channel correlations, bi-level optimization, and simultaneous point/subsequence anomaly detection with state-of-the-art performance. Updating the headline dataset count from 21 to 22 expands supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds an interpretation that CATCH's advantages persist for high-frequency anomalies and anomalies without distinct frequency-band separation, connecting the new observations to fine-grained modeling. Existing ablation and anomaly-score interpretations largely remain, without a substantial new limitations analysis.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 substantially expands reproducibility documentation with baseline architectures, hyperparameter ranges, and tuning information. Code access changes from an anonymous site to the named GitHub repository, and the dataset-download link changes. Existing scoring and TODS-generation code remain; the appendix's blanket L1-training statement is removed.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand their cited literature, including SparseTSF and recent forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly-detection studies. Rewritten Section 2.3 and new Table 1 explicitly position frequency methods by multivariate support, granularity alignment, high-frequency handling, and channel correlations.

P1.justification: The method narrative is extensively reorganized: correlation discovery moves into the CFM description, reconstruction receives a dedicated section, and optimization and scoring are explained separately. The introduction and related work expand, terminology is standardized, and numerous wording errors are corrected.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the architecture diagram, adds the related-work comparison table and Appendix D's table/figure, and reformats the ablation display. Benchmark tables gain ASD rows and TFAD columns. Appendix accuracy results are separated from precision/recall/F1 into their own table; existing plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves method clarity and baseline reproducibility documentation, while the TFAD comparison and controlled spectral study strengthen empirical support. These are useful incremental gains over the retained results. Reporting inconsistencies temper the improvement: v2 Table 7 credits CATCH with 65 wins despite at least three losses among 66 comparisons. Overall, the clearer explanation and additional evidence provide a limited net quality improvement.
